question: Which engine type is installed on the Boeing 737-800?
explanation: The Next Generation family is powered by the CFM56-7B. The CFM56-3 belongs to the Classic series and the LEAP-1B to the MAX.

question: How many floor level exits are provided for the passenger cabin?
explanation: Two exits at the front and two at the rear. Each is a full size door with an escape slide and counts as an emergency exit.

question: How many overwing emergency exits are fitted to the 737-800?

options.text: Two on the left side only

explanation: The longer -800 fuselage requires four overwing exits, whereas the shorter -700 is certified with only two.

question: On which side of the fuselage are the passenger entry doors located?

options.text: Forward on the left, aft on the right
Either side, depending on the operator

explanation: Entry doors are on the left and service doors on the right, which keeps passenger boarding separated from catering and cleaning.

question: What is the maximum certificated passenger seating capacity of the 737-800?
explanation: The limit is set by the number and type of emergency exits, not by the floor area of the cabin. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: What action arms the escape slide at a floor level door?

options.text: Engaging the girt bar in the floor fittings

explanation: With the girt bar attached to the floor, opening the door pulls the slide pack out and triggers inflation automatically.

question: What happens if an armed door is opened from outside by ground staff?

options.text: Nothing, external opening always disarms the slide
A warning horn sounds but the slide stays packed
The door cannot be opened at all

explanation: The slide has no way of knowing who opened the door, which is why disarming must be confirmed before any door is opened on arrival.

question: If automatic inflation fails after an armed door is opened, what means remains available?

options.text: A manual inflation handle on the slide
Compressed air from the pneumatic system
A second girt bar in the door frame
No alternative, the exit becomes unusable

explanation: The manual handle fires the inflation bottle directly, so a single failure of the automatic sequence does not lose the exit.

question: Where are the door warning lights displayed to the flight crew?

options.text: On the first officer side panel

explanation: They sit in the flight crew scan on the forward overhead panel, so an unlocked door is caught before taxi.

question: What does an illuminated door warning light indicate?

options.text: That the escape slide has inflated
That the door seal has failed
That the door is not closed and locked

explanation: The light monitors closure and locking only. It says nothing about the condition of the slide or the seal.

question: Does the flight deck door warning system show whether the escape slides are armed?

options.text: No, arming status is not indicated to the flight crew
Yes, an amber light shows each armed door
Yes, but only for the forward doors
Only when the parking brake is released

explanation: Arming can only be confirmed visually at the door, which is why the crew relies on a cabin crew report rather than a cockpit indication.

question: Besides passenger and cargo doors, which access is monitored by the door warning display?
explanation: An open equipment bay access affects pressurisation and airframe integrity, so it is monitored alongside the cabin doors.

question: Where are the cargo compartment doors located?

options.text: On the left side, forward and aft
Forward on the left, aft on the right
On the right side, forward and aft

explanation: Both cargo doors are on the right, opposite the passenger entry doors, so loading and boarding can proceed at the same time.

question: Why can a cabin door not normally be opened while residual cabin pressure remains?

options.text: Cabin pressure acting on the door holds it firmly against its stops
An electrical interlock prevents the handle from moving
The door is mechanically locked by the landing gear system
The door handle is disabled until the engines are shut down

explanation: Even a small differential produces a very large force over the door area, which is why pressurisation must be confirmed zero before opening.

question: How does an overwing exit operate on the Next Generation?

options.text: The hatch must be pulled inboard and placed on a seat
Pulling the handle opens the hatch outward and upward automatically
The hatch slides forward into the fuselage skin
The hatch is jettisoned by a pyrotechnic charge

explanation: The automatic hatch removes the need for a passenger to handle a heavy panel, which speeds up evacuation through the overwing exits.

question: Which flight deck windows can be opened?

options.text: The No. 2 sliding windows on both sides
The No. 3 windows on both sides

explanation: Each pilot has an openable No. 2 sliding window. The windshields and the aft side windows are fixed.

question: Apart from ground ventilation, what is the function of the flight deck sliding windows?

options.text: They provide an emergency exit for the flight crew
They allow manual de-icing of the windshield
They serve as a static pressure source
They allow smoke to be vented in flight

explanation: They are the flight crew emergency exit when the flight deck door or cabin is unusable after an accident.

question: Where are the flight deck escape straps stowed?

options.text: In the ceiling above each sliding window

explanation: Stowing them directly above the exit lets the crew anchor and deploy a strap without leaving the escape route.

question: What is the purpose of the decompression panels in the flight deck door?

options.text: To allow the cabin crew to pass documents through
To ventilate the flight deck on the ground
To open during a rapid decompression and equalise pressure across the door
To provide access if the electronic lock fails

explanation: Without them the pressure difference across the door during a rapid decompression could damage the door and its frame.

question: What are the positions of the flight deck door lock selector?
explanation: UNLKD releases the lock immediately, AUTO UNLK allows the delayed access sequence, and DENY blocks access attempts.

question: What does selecting DENY achieve?

options.text: It unlocks the door immediately for cabin crew
It inhibits keypad access attempts for a preset period
It disables the flight deck door chime only
It locks the door mechanically until maintenance action

explanation: It gives the crew a positive way to refuse entry when an access attempt is considered a threat.

question: With the selector in AUTO UNLK, what happens after a correct code is entered and the crew does not respond?

options.text: The door unlocks after a time delay
The door unlocks only if the autopilot is engaged
An alarm sounds in the cabin

explanation: The delayed unlock is the safeguard against both pilots being incapacitated, since the cabin crew can still gain entry.

question: What is the effect on the flight deck door lock of losing its electrical power?

options.text: The lock remains engaged until power is restored
The door locks and the keypad is disabled

explanation: The lock is designed fail safe so that a power loss cannot trap the crew or block access to the flight deck.

question: How is the flight crew alerted that someone has entered a code on the flight deck door keypad?

options.text: By a chime and an indication on the door panel
By the cabin interphone call light only

explanation: The chime and light draw attention to the request so the crew can decide before the automatic sequence completes.

question: Where is the emergency lighting switch located?

options.text: On the aft overhead panel under a guard
At the forward flight attendant station

explanation: It is guarded to prevent an inadvertent selection that would leave the system unarmed.

question: What are the positions of the emergency lighting switch?
explanation: ARMED is the normal position for flight, giving automatic operation while leaving the lights extinguished.

question: With the switch at ARMED, what causes the emergency lights to illuminate automatically?

options.text: Selection of flaps to the landing setting
Cabin altitude exceeding the warning value

explanation: A loss of normal DC power is treated as the signature of an accident or major failure, so the escape path lighting comes on by itself.

question: When does the EMER EXIT LIGHT NOT ARMED light illuminate?

options.text: When the switch is not in the ARMED position
When any emergency light has failed
When the emergency light batteries are discharged
During the emergency light test only

explanation: It is a configuration reminder, so the crew does not depart with the system unable to operate automatically.

question: From what source do the emergency lights operate after a total loss of airplane power?

options.text: Dedicated battery packs in the lighting system

explanation: Independent battery packs mean the escape lighting survives even the loss of the airplane battery itself.

question: For approximately how long must the emergency lights operate on their own power?
explanation: The duration is set to cover evacuation and the period immediately after it. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: Which of the following forms part of the emergency lighting system?
explanation: Low level marking remains visible when smoke fills the upper cabin, which is when overhead lighting becomes useless.

question: On which frequencies does the emergency locator transmitter broadcast?
explanation: The 406 MHz signal is received by satellite for position reporting, while the older frequencies support homing by search aircraft.

question: How is the emergency locator transmitter activated automatically?

options.text: By cabin altitude exceeding its limit

explanation: The g switch fires on the deceleration of an impact, so the transmitter operates even if the crew is incapacitated.

question: Where is the flight deck control switch for the emergency locator transmitter?
explanation: Its position on the aft overhead keeps it clear of the normal operating panels while remaining reachable from the seat.

question: What is the purpose of protective breathing equipment?

options.text: To supply oxygen at high cabin altitudes
To replace the crew oxygen mask during a decompression
To protect the eyes and airway and supply oxygen while fighting a fire in smoke

explanation: It is a firefighting item. Unlike the oxygen mask it seals the whole head, so smoke cannot reach the eyes or the airway.

question: Approximately how long does protective breathing equipment provide protection once activated?
explanation: The duration governs how the crew plans a firefighting attempt. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: Why is Halon used for the flight deck extinguisher rather than water?

options.text: It can be discharged without depressurising the cabin
It is effective on electrical and flammable liquid fires and leaves no residue
It cools the fire faster than water

explanation: Water conducts and would damage the avionics, whereas Halon smothers the fire without contaminating the equipment.

question: What is the principal restriction on the use of a water extinguisher?

options.text: It must not be used on electrical or flammable liquid fires
It must not be used above 10000 ft cabin altitude
It must not be used in the cabin
It must not be used while the engines are running

explanation: Water conducts electricity and spreads burning liquids, so the class of fire has to be identified before the extinguisher is selected.

question: Where is the crash axe stowed?
explanation: It is stowed where the crew can reach panels and structure from inside the flight deck after an accident.

question: What is the purpose of the portable oxygen bottles carried in the cabin?

options.text: They are a backup to the passenger oxygen system during a decompression
They provide first aid oxygen and allow crew members to move about the cabin
They supply the protective breathing equipment
They feed the flight deck masks if the fixed supply fails

explanation: They are therapeutic and mobility items. They are not sized or plumbed to replace the fixed passenger system.

question: Why are megaphones carried on board?

options.text: To direct passengers during an evacuation when the public address system is unavailable
To communicate with ground personnel during pushback
To pass cabin reports to the flight deck

explanation: After a power loss or ditching the address system may be dead, and command of the evacuation still has to be heard the length of the cabin.

question: What do smoke goggles provide that an oxygen mask alone does not?

options.text: Eye protection from smoke and irritants

explanation: The mask protects breathing only, so without goggles the eyes remain exposed and the crew may be unable to see the instruments.

question: What is the approximate overall length of the 737-800?
explanation: Length matters for stand allocation and manoeuvring clearance. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: What is the approximate wingspan of a 737-800 fitted with blended winglets?
explanation: Winglets add roughly a metre and a half of span, which can affect gate and taxiway compatibility. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: What is the approximate height of the 737-800 at the top of the fin?
explanation: Tail height is the limiting dimension for hangar and jetway clearance. Verify against your operator FCOM.

question: What is the main aerodynamic benefit of blended winglets?

options.text: They increase the maximum lift coefficient at low speed
They reduce induced drag, improving climb performance and fuel burn
They increase directional stability at high Mach number
They reduce the stalling speed in the landing configuration

explanation: By weakening the wingtip vortex they reduce the drag due to lift, which is why the benefit is greatest in the climb and at high weights.

question: Where is the electronics and equipment compartment access located?

options.text: In the aft cargo compartment ceiling

explanation: Placing the compartment forward and below the cabin floor keeps the avionics close to the flight deck and accessible from the ground.

question: What are the positions of the passenger seat belt sign switch?
explanation: AUTO links the sign to the airplane configuration, while OFF and ON give the crew direct manual control.

question: With the seat belt sign switch in AUTO, what causes the signs to illuminate?

options.text: Cabin altitude rising above the warning value
The position of the landing gear and flaps

explanation: The configuration is used as the signal that the airplane is in a low level phase of flight. Verify the exact logic against your operator FCOM.

question: What is the effect of cycling the seat belt sign switch?

options.text: It sounds a chime that alerts the cabin crew
It resets the cabin call system

explanation: Cycling the switch is a recognised way of passing a prearranged signal to the cabin crew without using the interphone.

question: How many observer seats may be installed on the flight deck?
explanation: The first observer seat is standard and a second may be fitted as an option, which is relevant to crew and inspector carriage.

question: Why is a flashlight stowed at each crew station and checked before flight?

options.text: To provide light for evacuation and firefighting if the normal lighting fails
To inspect the cargo compartments during turnaround
To signal to ground personnel during pushback
To illuminate the circuit breaker panels in normal operations

explanation: Smoke and a loss of power can leave the cabin dark, so a serviceable flashlight within reach of the seat is part of the equipment check.
